A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IM360's spherical SfM, geometry reconstruction, and texture optimization pipeline. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the revised title and reorganized supplementary material.

before.justification: V1 reports original camera-registration, pose-estimation, rendering, and ablation results in Tables 1–3, with additional qualitative results in its appendix.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds multi-floor localization results, an Insta360 house demonstration, and qualitative geometry comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 revises the stated bundle-adjustment objective: v1 specifies Huber loss, whereas v3 specifies soft L1 for local adjustment and no robustifier globally. The overall pipeline remains unchanged. V3 newly documents match quantization, but does not establish that quantization was absent from the earlier implementation.

E1.justification: V3 retains the original Matterport3D and Stanford2D3D evaluations and adds two multi-floor Matterport3D scenes and a custom house captured with an Insta360 camera. These extend building-layout and sensor coverage within the existing indoor-mapping task. Other datasets listed in the new Table 4 are contextual comparisons, not additional evaluation datasets.

E2.justification: V3 adds qualitative surface-reconstruction comparisons against SuGaR and VCR-GauS in Figures 3 and 11. OmniSDF's failure was already reported in v1. The camera-localization and rendering comparator sets in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged; newly cited matchers such as SPHORB are not reported as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The original benchmark selections, image resolutions, training budgets, and evaluation metrics are retained. Added evaluations introduce a 20-image capture of a 56-square-meter house and full-building localization with 89 and 116 input views. These are additional experimental configurations, not revisions to the original benchmark protocols.

E4.justification: V3 adds a multi-floor robustness check, a practical consumer-camera case study, and qualitative analyses of Gaussian-splatting surface-reconstruction failures supporting the choice of DebSDF. The existing two-view-initialization and diffuse-versus-specular texture ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. V1's Gaussian-process covariance equations describe the matcher, not uncertainty in the reported experimental results.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. V3 Figure 7 adds 89/89 registrations with AUC@5 of 71.48 for a two-story scene and 116/116 with 48.37 for a three-story scene. The custom-house reconstruction and SuGaR/VCR-GauS failure examples add qualitative outcomes; they do not demonstrate gains over v1 under identical conditions.

T1.justification: The definition of the bundle-adjustment penalty changes from Huber to soft L1 locally and an unrobustified global objective. Other mathematical edits mainly expand existing formulations: Appendix 7 spells out the spherical eight-point linear system and DebSDF depth/normal losses, while v1's borrowed Gaussian-process equations are omitted. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a unified pipeline for sparse indoor reconstruction, spherical SfM using dense matching, and improved rendering through diffuse/specular texture optimization. V3 promotes the 3.5-PSNR advantage into its abstract, but that result and the principal superiority and novelty claims already appear in v1.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly acknowledges that geometric reconstruction deteriorates beyond a certain scene scale and explains why image retrieval is excluded to isolate other pipeline components. It also interprets the added geometry failures as support for DebSDF. V1's limitations instead emphasize mesh-error sensitivity and future joint geometry/texture optimization, although geometric-inaccuracy concerns remain elsewhere in v3.

D1.justification: New Appendix 7 documents confidence filtering, grid-based match quantization, spherical eight-point construction, and explicit depth/normal loss terms. The original architecture and optimization hyperparameters are retained. The project-page address changes from an anonymous site to the named IM360 site; the PDFs alone do not establish additional resource availability.

R1.justification: V3 adds references supporting match quantization, spherical features, Gaussian surface reconstruction, and the broader indoor-dataset comparison. Its positioning against SuGaR and VCR-GauS is new, while the main related-work narrative and novelty claims remain stable. The updated EDM reference identifies the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: V3 shortens the title, rewrites the abstract and selected method/limitations passages, and reorganizes the supplement into application, technical-detail, and experimental sections. Some geometry exposition moves from the main text to the appendix, references move to the end, and broken supplementary citations are repaired. Most introductory and experimental prose is retained.

P2.justification: V3 substantially revises the visual exposition: it combines and rearranges the pipeline diagrams, moves the detailed geometry schematic into the appendix, and augments Figure 1 with dataset-density statistics. New displays cover geometry failures, multi-floor localization, the custom capture, and dataset characteristics. Existing qualitative appendix panels are retained and renumbered, with review-copy headers removed.

improvement.justification: V3 improves technical transparency and traceability through the expanded appendix and repaired citations. The multi-floor and consumer-camera demonstrations provide useful additional applicability evidence, while the revised limitations acknowledge reconstruction-scale constraints. These gains are limited: Tables 1–3 remain unchanged, and the added geometry comparisons are qualitative with little experimental detail. The evidence supports a modest overall improvement.
